pr.title: Derive library KGs for referenced IRIS items without holding their PDFs
pr.body:
Refs #207, #213.

## What

As the owner asked on 2026-11-10: "retrieve PDF/source document locally, run KG ingestion routines/derivative KGs. store those but do not materialize original asset on the KG", and "do all 144".

- **New script `scripts/iris-cdn/derive-referenced.py`.** It turns each ORIGINAL PDF into one library entry.
  - The English PDF becomes `library/<stem>`; other language versions become `library/<stem>-<lang>`.
  - The OCR language hint comes from the file name, or else from `dc.language.iso`.
  - The PDF, page images and figures are discarded. The bitstream stays `referenced` and records a sha256 of the bytes that were read.
- **186 PDFs derived**, from the 144 referenced items plus two new subsets: six-language sets, and digital-health documents with official WHO translations. All six UN languages are represented: en 99, fr 34, ru 20, zh 12, es 11, ar 10 (counted by script and word frequency over the derived sections).
- **Masked covers for the 26 new items** (masks in `scripts/iris-covers/masks.json`, each checked by eye).
- **Guard against bad downloads.** `fetch-referenced-pdfs.py` and `derive-referenced.py` now refuse a download that is not a PDF. IRIS served an HTML sign-in page for 10665/67211 (fr); that item was refetched and re-derived.
- About 81 MB of derived files.

## Depends on

litlfred/cat-harness-tools#1787: language-aware OCR, plus text-layer checks that send unreadable text to OCR. The checks catch mojibake, reversed Arabic ligatures, and a text layer in the wrong script (as in 10665/69384, Arabic edition). It also adds `--qa-later`. After it merges, who-iris needs a re-pin.

## Checks

- `bun run check:catalogue` ✓
- `bun run iris:covers:check` ✓ (172 covers)
- `bun run dc:render` and `bun run iris:pages` were rerun.
- `bun test ./scripts/tests/`: 96 pass.

Image descriptions for the new entries are left for later (`--qa-later`).
